summary: Feed s147_double to IDS is degraded: tool port overloaded by ~196% microbursts (1.96 Gbps vs 1 Gbps) and encrypted traffic share (63.7%) exceeds IDS tolerance (60%), reducing inspection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering bursty aggregated traffic to a single 1 Gbps IDS port without load balancing or shaping. 1ms peaks hit 1.96 Gbps (196% of port capacity) across 8 intervals, indicating microbursts that exceed line rate.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS ingress buffer overruns and silently drops packets during bursts; IDS misses flows/signatures, creates detection gaps and incomplete session reassembly despite needing both directions and full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 2-3 IDS ports/instances with flow-aware hashing to keep per-port peak <0.8 Gbps and preserve bidirectional flow symmetry required by IDS.

findings.root_cause: 63.7% of bytes are encrypted (TLS) vs 60% IDS tolerance. Traffic mix has shifted to mostly encrypted, and no upstream decryption/visibility is applied before the IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload for signature matching but cannot inspect encrypted payloads; ~64% of traffic is opaque, significantly reducing detection coverage for threats inside TLS.

params.policy: decrypt relevant categories, bypass trusted privacy-sensitive flows

recommended_fix.why: IDS cannot detect inside encryption. Adding selective decryption at the packet broker / SSL visibility layer before the IDS will restore payload visibility while staying within privacy policy, or alternatively filter known-trusted encrypted flows to bring share below 60%.
